summary: Prettier quadratic CPU consumption when formatting GFM Markdown tables
description:
### Summary

Prettier's Markdown parser (parser `"markdown"`, also reached through `"mdx"` table content) ships a bundled `micromark-extension-gfm-table` whose `EditMap` resolves event edits by linearly scanning an in-memory array on every edit. A GFM table with `N` body rows triggers `O(N)` edits, each scanning an `O(N)` list (plus an `O(N)` event slice per edit in `consume()`), so formatting time grows as `O(N²)`.

A ~40 KB Markdown document that is a single GFM table with 4,000 rows takes ~1.1 s to format, whereas a paragraph of the identical byte size takes ~65 ms. Doubling the row count roughly quadruples the time. Because Prettier is embedded in countless online formatters, playgrounds, and review/comment widgets that turn untrusted Markdown into HTML or formatted text, an attacker can send a small (~100–300 KB) Markdown payload that pins a CPU core for tens of seconds. There is no error, no malformed input required — the table is valid CommonMark/GFM.

No prototype-pollution vector was found; this is an availability (algorithmic-complexity) issue only.

### Details

- Affected package: `prettier` (npm), version **3.9.9** (latest stable), commit **cdd17f2288b28b170a76416c72dac56e3ea5daff** ("Release 3.9.9", 2026-09-23). Node v22.23.2, macOS arm64.
- The Markdown parser was newly migrated to `micromark` in Prettier 3.9.0 (2026-06-27); this code path is new and had not been load-tested against adversarial table shapes.
- Bundled dependency: `micromark-extension-gfm-table@2.1.1` (pinned in Prettier's lockfile). The linear-scan `EditMap.add` is the root cause.
- Root cause file/line (upstream source of the bundled code): `micromark-extension-gfm-table/lib/edit-map.js`, function `addImplementation`, the `while (index < editMap.map.length)` linear scan (≈ lines 132–153), compounded by the reverse-iteration `events.slice()` loop in `consume()` (≈ lines 98–119).
- Root cause in the Prettier bundle: `node_modules/prettier/plugins/markdown.mjs`, line 33. The minified `EditMap` class is `var Kr=class{constructor(){this.map=[]}add(t,r,n){sd(this,t,r,n)}consume(t){...}}` (ctor at line 33 col 22432) and the linear-scan inserter is `function sd(e,t,r,n){...for(;a<e.map.length;){if(e.map[a][0]===t){...}a+=1}e.map.push([t,r,n])}` (line 33 col 22793). The table `resolveAll` function `cd(...)` allocates `p=new Kr` and calls `p.add(...)` once per cell boundary per row.
- Why it is quadratic: for a table with `N` rows, `cd`/`Qr`/`ro` issue `~4N` `add()` calls. Each `add` scans the entire `map` array (which grows to `O(N)`) to dedupe edits at a given index → `O(N²)` comparisons. `consume()` then iterates the `O(N)` edits in reverse, calling `events.slice(...)` (an `O(events.length)` copy) each time → a second `O(N²)` term.
- Sibling surface checked: the same `EditMap` is used only by GFM tables. Plain nested links/images (`[[[...x...]]]`) show a much milder linear-in-N² term in core `micromark` (≈10× smaller constant; ~150 ms at N=6,400) and are not reported here as a separate issue. The `less`/`postcss-less` parser showed a superlinear signal in isolation but it originates in `postcss-less` itself and is not reachable through Prettier's bundled version with a smaller constant; not included.
- Prototype pollution: canaries planted on `Object.prototype` and fed `__proto__`/`constructor.prototype` keys across JSON, YAML, babel, graphql, glimmer, html, css parsers did not result in pollution of a fresh object.

### Tested patch
The following patch was tested before reporting:

```diff
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 (prettier bundled micromark-extension-gfm-table 2.1.1)
Subject: [PATCH] perf(markdown): make GFM table EditMap add O(1) instead of O(n)

The bundled micromark-extension-gfm-table EditMap resolved edits by linearly
scanning `map` for a matching index on every `add()` call. A table with N
rows issues O(N) edits, each scanning an O(N)-length array, making table
parsing O(N^2). A second O(N) factor comes from the per-edit
`events.slice()` inside `consume()`.

This change keys edits by index in a Map, mirroring the upstream fix
(shipped in micromark-extension-gfm-table 2.1.2). Output is byte-identical.

---
 src/language-markdown/parse/micromark/edit-map.js (derived) | 16 ++++++++------
 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/edit-map.js b/edit-map.js
--- a/edit-map.js
+++ b/edit-map.js
@@ -34,6 +34,11 @@ export class EditMap {
      * @type {Array<Change>}
      */
     this.map = [];
+
+    /**
+     * Changes by index, so `add` does not scan `map`.
+     * @type {Map<number, Change>}
+     */
+    this.index = new Map();
   }
 ...
@@ -132,21 +137,17 @@ function addImplementation(editMap, at, remove, add) {
   if (remove === 0 && add.length === 0) {
     return;
   }
-  let index = 0;
-  while (index < editMap.map.length) {
-    if (editMap.map[index][0] === at) {
-      editMap.map[index][1] += remove;
-      editMap.map[index][2].push(...add);
-      return;
-    }
-    index += 1;
-  }
-  editMap.map.push([at, remove, add]);
+  const existing = editMap.index.get(at);
+  if (existing) {
+    existing[1] += remove;
+    existing[2].push(...add);
+    return;
+  }
+  const change = [at, remove, add];
+  editMap.map.push(change);
+  editMap.index.set(at, change);
 }
 ...
   // in consume(), after `this.map.length = 0;` add:
+  this.index.clear();

Release note:
  Markdown: fix quadratic (O(n^2)) CPU usage when formatting GFM tables with
  many rows. A table of N rows now parses in O(N) instead of O(N^2); output
  is unchanged. Upgrades bundled micromark-extension-gfm-table to 2.1.2.
```


### Proof of concept

Environment: Node v22.23.2, `prettier@3.9.9` from npm, `prettier.format(code, { parser: "markdown" })`.

Exploit input (4,000-row GFM table, ~40 KB):

```
| a | b |
|---|---|
| x | y |
| x | y |
...   (4,000 identical rows)
```

Control (paragraph of identical byte length, ~40 KB): `word word word ...`

Measured wall time (pre-patch, captured):

| N (rows) | Exploit table (ms) | Control paragraph (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 500 | 44 | 14 |
| 1,000 | 104 | 22 |
| 2,000 | 309 | 37 |
| 4,000 | 1,079 | 66 |
| 8,000 | 4,087 | 113 |

Doubling N → ~3.5–4× time (constant `ms/N² ≈ 4e-5`); control grows linearly (~2×). A 25,600-row table (~250 KB) exceeds ~40 s on one core.

Post-patch (applying the fix below — keying `EditMap` edits by index in a `Map`):

| N (rows) | Exploit table (ms) post-patch |
|---:|---:|
| 500 | 32 |
| 1,000 | 58 |
| 2,000 | 81 |
| 4,000 | 157 |
| 8,000 | 360 |

Doubling N → ~2× (linear). At N=8,000 the table format time dropped from 4,087 ms to 360 ms (≈11×). Output on the exploit and on a representative table corpus was verified **byte-identical** (112,028 bytes matched exactly before/after).

A runnable harness (`poc.js`, `verify-identical.js`) and the raw timing tables are in the artifacts directory.

### Impact

- Availability denial: a single small HTTP request to an online Prettier-based Markdown formatter/playground pins a worker CPU core for seconds-to-minutes. A handful of concurrent such requests exhausts the formatter's worker pool, denying service to legitimate users.
- Confidentiality and integrity are unaffected; no code execution, no information disclosure, no prototype pollution.
- The payload is valid, syntactically correct GFM — no fuzzing/crash conditions, no parser error — so it passes through normal input filters.
- Scope of affected users: anyone exposing Prettier's Markdown parser to untrusted input (playgrounds, issue/comment renderers, docs pipelines, shared format-as-a-service).
